headline: No penalty for Hülkenberg after impeding Sainz in qualifying
body: Hülkenberg received no penalty after blocking Sainz's push lap at Turn 5. Inconsistent timing information had led both teams to believe Sainz had already taken the chequered flag, leaving Audi no reasonable chance to correct its message to Hülkenberg.

headline: Hadjar cleared to start the Singapore Grand Prix
body: Hadjar has been granted permission to start the Singapore Grand Prix.

headline: Pirelli favours a soft-tyre start and one stop in Singapore
body: Pirelli expects the soft tyre's early grip to make it the preferred starting compound, followed by medium or hard tyres. Low degradation could let drivers extend the opening stint while waiting for a Safety Car; a two-stop race is estimated to be around ten seconds slower than the one-stop options.

headline: Verstappen questions second-gear starts after wet-race struggles
body: Verstappen started the wet Sepang race and Singapore sprint in second gear on Red Bull's advice, but says that approach is not working well enough. He would consider a different gear if Sunday's start is wet, while hoping for a dry race.

headline: Russell says repaired Mercedes felt different in qualifying
body: Russell qualified sixth after Mercedes repaired his sprint crash damage, but said the car no longer felt as it had on Friday. He is trying to understand the loss of pace and expects a difficult recovery from the back of the grid on a track where passing is hard.

headline: Hamilton calls for Singapore track changes to help overtaking
body: Hamilton wants a longer straight and further layout changes at Marina Bay to create better overtaking chances. Verstappen and Leclerc also questioned holding sprints at circuits where passing is so difficult; no circuit change has been announced.

headline: Provisional starting grid for the Singapore Grand Prix
body: Verstappen and Leclerc share the front row, ahead of Hamilton and Antonelli. Russell starts 21st with a 40-place power-unit penalty, alongside Hadjar, who has permission to race. The FIA's provisional grid keeps Hülkenberg tenth; later car changes may still alter the starting order.
